subject: Anthropology
title: Debt and Obligation
description: A quick win: understand Debt and Obligation.

hook.text: Before banks, there was debt. You owed your neighbor grain, your chief loyalty, and your gods sacrifice.

buildup.text: Debt is a moral and economic relationship. Owing creates obligation, hierarchy, and dependence between people.

discovery.text: Graeber showed that debt is older than money. Entire civilizations organized around credit systems, not cash exchange.

twist.text: Debt can enslave. Throughout history, inability to pay debts has led to bondage, dispossession, and social death.

climax.text: Debt is never just financial. It's moral, social, and political. Who owes whom defines the shape of every society.

punchline.text: Debt built civilizations and destroyed them.

quiz.question: What did Graeber argue about debt?
options: Debt was invented by modern banks
Debt is older than money and organized entire civilizations

details.summary: Debt in anthropological perspective is not merely financial but a fundamental social relationship of obligation. David Graeber argued that debt preceded money, structured social hierarchies, and has been used throughout history to control, exploit, and morally dominate debtors.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding debt as a social power relationship rather than just a financial contract reveals why debt crises are moral crises. Debt shame, debtor prisons, and austerity politics all make sense when debt is seen as a tool of social control.
takeaways: Debt is a social relationship of obligation, not just a financial one
Graeber argued that debt preceded money historically
Debt has been used as a tool of social control throughout history

faq.question: How can debt be seen as a form of social control?
faq.answer: Indebted people are controllable — they must work for creditors, accept unfavorable terms, and cannot resist. Debt bondage enslaved millions historically. Student loans, mortgages, and national debt continue to structure power relations between creditors and debtors at every scale.

faq.question: What is the relationship between debt and morality?
faq.answer: Debt carries intense moral weight — being in debt means owing, and failure to repay is treated as a moral failing. Yet Graeber showed that the powerful have always defaulted without shame while the poor are moralized into repaying. The moral language of debt is applied asymmetrically.
